raw_response:
I will keep my land in the local winter wheat and summer maize rotation. In Quzhou, this is still the steadiest grain pattern, the summer rain matches maize well, and winter wheat can still make good use of irrigation and fertilizer. I would not switch into cotton or vegetables this year because I am 58, I want a simpler system with lower labor pressure, and I would rather chase stable grain yield than take on more market and management risk. I will run one 10 mu block through the full year: winter wheat first, then summer maize on the same land after harvest. For wheat, I will use an improved variety, put more water into the dry season, and keep fertilizer moderate instead of pushing too hard. For maize, I will use a hybrid, rely mainly on summer rainfall, and keep one irrigation in reserve. I will also keep pesticide use controlled and practical, and I will use rotary tillage for wheat and no-tillage for maize so I can turn the field around fast after the wheat harvest. This matches what has worked locally in Quzhou, where wheat-maize rotation dominates and recent county demonstration fields showed strong yields with about 14 kg N per mu on wheat and about 13.8 kg N per mu on maize, with fewer irrigations than the older high-input pattern.

Sources: [Ministry of Agriculture report on Quzhou grain area](https://www.moa.gov.cn/xw/qg/202107/t20210720_6372348.htm), [China Agricultural University Quzhou Station 2024 demo results](https://qzsyz.cau.edu.cn/art/2024/10/8/art_46317_1039835.html), [Quzhou winter wheat-summer maize system background](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5290742/)
